evidence: Wikipedia's article on Jay-Z: 'Reasonable Doubt' (1996) included beats from DJ Premier and Clark Kent.

trackPair.whatToListenFor: Premier gave Nas a dark piano loop and hard drums. On 'D'Evils' he gives Jay-Z the same kind of thing: a short, minor-key loop, scratched vocal fragments in the chorus, and drums that hit hard and plainly. Listen to the two beats one after the other: two different Brooklyn and Queens rappers on very similar ground.

explanation.age13: DJ Premier, who had produced Nas's best-known songs, also made beats for Jay-Z's first album in 1996.
explanation.adult: Premier's production ties together Nas, Jay-Z and Biggie, the three New York rappers whose rivalries shaped the late 1990s.
